what: Spotify is the largest music streaming service outside China. Users pay a monthly subscription or listen free with advertising, and the company pays most of what it collects to record labels, publishers and podcast creators.
customers: Consumers in most countries; advertisers buying audio and video ads against free listeners.
money: monthly plans for individuals, families, students and duos
audio, video and podcast advertising shown to free users
moat: The largest audience in streaming audio, recommendation systems trained on years of listening, and playlists that users build and do not want to recreate elsewhere.
risks: Record labels own the music and take most of each subscription
Apple, Amazon and Google can bundle music into services people already pay for
Price increases risk slowing subscriber growth
Podcast and audiobook investments have not always paid back
opportunities: Price rises have flowed through with little subscriber loss, lifting margins
Audiobooks and a higher-priced tier can raise revenue per user
Advertising is a small share of revenue and could grow if podcast monetisation improves
watch: Monthly active users and premium subscribers, and gross margin, which shows how much it keeps after paying rights holders.
